clue.text: Pain from exercise in saddle perhaps

definitions.meaning: a sharp pain in the side that runners get
a single loop of thread, as found in leatherwork such as a saddle

explanation.surface: A rider complains of a pain that comes from long hours of exercise in the saddle.
explanation.definitionFit: Both senses are standard: the side-pain of exertion and a loop of thread sewn into leather.

clue.text: Portia rarely displays luxurious headgear

indicators.note: displays says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Portia from The Merchant of Venice seldom shows off a fancy hat.
explanation.definitionFit: A jewelled ornamental crown or headband worn by royalty or brides is costly headwear.

clue.text: Trollope novel in Churchill's retreat?

definitions.meaning: Anthony Trollope's 1855 novel, first of the Barsetshire series
read as ..., the private room where a wartime leader might hole up

explanation.surface: A Victorian novel is set in Winston Churchill's private hideaway.
explanation.walkthrough: The second sense splits into three words: a den, a private retreat, for running the war.
explanation.definitionFit: Trollope's novel about Septimus Harding of Hiram's Hospital; the question mark flags the punning second sense.

clue.text: Big actor falling short — that is what you need for a sad movie

definitions.text: what you need for a sad movie

indicators.note: falling short means coming up one letter short, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: Tom Hanks, who starred in the film Big
i.e. is the abbreviation of id est, Latin for that is

explanation.surface: A big-name actor's performance disappoints, leaving the audience needing tissues at a weepie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Big' reads as famous, but it is the 1988 film starring Tom Hanks.
explanation.definitionFit: A handkerchief, informally, is what you reach for to dry tears in a tear-jerker.

clue.text: Detectives must probe old coin in the West

indicators.note: to probe is to push into something, so the detectives go inside the other letters

parts.note: a cent is a small coin
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, the British police detectives

explanation.surface: Police detectives investigate an old coin turned up somewhere out west.
explanation.definitionFit: The Occident is a literary name for the Western world, opposite the Orient.

clue.text: What can make email bounce between two cricket sides very rarely

indicators.note: between puts the jumbled letters with one side before and one after

parts.note: the on side is the leg side of a cricket field; two of them give a pair of on-sides
the second on side

indicators.note: what can make suggests the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Emails bounce between two teams in a cricket match only on rare occasions.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bounce' looks like the anagram signal but is part of the fodder; 'What can make' is the signal. In cricket the on side is the leg side.
explanation.definitionFit: An idiom for something happening almost never, from the rarity of a second full moon in a month.

clue.text: Revolutionary Nazi guard — knight perhaps

parts.note: Che Guevara, the Argentine-born Marxist revolutionary
an SS man was a member of the Nazi Schutzstaffel

explanation.surface: A revolutionary and a Nazi guard are compared to a chivalrous knight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Knight' suggests armour, but it is a piece on the board.
explanation.definitionFit: A knight is one example of a piece used in the board game of kings and queens.

clue.text: Exclude society girl meeting a queen

parts.note: a deb, short for debutante, is a young woman entering high society
R is short for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: A debutante is shut out when she meets a queen.
explanation.definitionFit: To debar is to bar or ban someone from taking part.

clue.text: Cook big lunch with last of brisket joint for latecomers

indicators.note: to cook can mean to tamper with or juggle, so these letters are rearranged
last of picks out the final letter of the following word

explanation.surface: A recipe for a big lunch using the end of a brisket joint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Joint' looks like the brisket, but it is a slang word for a venue, here a late-night one.
explanation.definitionFit: A joint is slang for an establishment; a venue open late at night suits those who arrive late.

clue.text: Place of worship gets a celebrant excited

indicators.note: excited means stirred up, so the letters of the fodder are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: A priest gets carried away with enthusiasm in church.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabernacle is a sanctuary, a building or tent used for religious worship.

clue.text: Secures trousers

definitions.meaning: to secure something, such as a seat or a prize, by claiming it first
an old informal word for loose-fitting trousers, as in Oxford ones

explanation.surface: Someone fastens their trousers.
explanation.definitionFit: A verb for claiming or grabbing something, and a dated plural noun for wide trousers.

clue.text: Someone lacking faith in one violinist

parts.note: a pagan is a heathen, someone outside the main religions
taken as written
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A violin virtuoso is described as having no religious belief.
explanation.definitionFit: Niccolò Paganini was the celebrated nineteenth-century Italian virtuoso of the violin.

clue.text: Goblin has ill feeling about king

indicators.note: about means going round, so the ill feeling surrounds the king

parts.note: spite is malice or ill will
R is short for Rex, Latin for king

explanation.surface: A goblin bears a grudge against the king.
explanation.definitionFit: A goblin and this word are both kinds of mischievous fairy or elf in folklore.

clue.text: American education put into employment

parts.note: US is short for United States, so American

explanation.surface: An American teaching qualification is finally given a job.
explanation.definitionFit: To put something into employment is to employ it; the past participle matches.

clue.text: Pot caused rogue to be this?

definitions.text: Pot caused rogue to be this?

indicators.note: rogue means behaving erratically and out of control, so the letters break out of order

explanation.surface: Smoking pot left a rascal in a state of drugged vagueness.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rogue' looks like the person getting high, but it signals the jumble; the whole clue also describes the stoned result.
explanation.definitionFit: Being dazed and out of touch, as cannabis use can leave someone, is to be vague and absent.

clue.text: Drink humorously described in a manuscript penned by a dramatic diarist

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: penned means shut in, as in a pen, so the first pieces sit inside the diarist

parts.note: Mrs Dale, the diary-keeping heroine of the long-running BBC radio drama Mrs Dale's Diary
taken as written

explanation.surface: A drink is mentioned in a manuscript written by a theatrical diary-keeper.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dramatic diarist' tempts towards Pepys, but it is Mrs Dale of the BBC radio serial Mrs Dale's Diary (1948-69); 'penned by' puts the first pieces inside her.
explanation.definitionFit: Adam's ale is a jocular name for water, the only drink available to the first man.

clue.text: Corporation to relieve Levantine city

parts.note: to spare someone a burden is to relieve them of it
Tyre is an ancient port city in Lebanon, in the Levant

explanation.surface: A company sets out to bring aid to a city in the Middle East.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Corporation' is an old humorous word for a pot belly, not a company.
explanation.definitionFit: A roll of fat around the waist is jokingly likened to an extra wheel carried in a car's boot.

clue.text: Meat that's cooked soft with butter in sparkling wine

parts.note: p is the musical abbreviation for piano, soft

indicators.note: in places the butter inside the sparkling wine

parts.note: Asti is a sparkling Italian wine from Piedmont
a ram butts with its head, so it is a butter

explanation.surface: A recipe: meat cooked gently with butter in fizzy wine.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Butter' is not the dairy spread but something that butts, a ram.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastrami is seasoned, smoked and cooked beef, served sliced.

clue.text: Animal is tangled in yacht's propeller

indicators.note: tangled means twisted up, so the letters of these two words are mixed together

explanation.surface: A creature gets caught up in the workings of a yacht.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Propeller' suggests a screw below the waterline, but a yacht is driven by wind on its biggest sail.
explanation.definitionFit: The principal sail of a vessel is what drives, or propels, a sailing yacht.

clue.text: Pop group once providing their own backing

indicators.note: the name, written backwards, is unchanged, so it backs itself up

parts.note: these definition words give the whole answer, and the answer is itself the palindrome: it reads the same from either end

explanation.surface: A former pop group sang their own backing vocals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Backing' sounds like backing singers, but it means read backwards: the group's name is a palindrome.
explanation.definitionFit: The Swedish quartet who won Eurovision in 1974 split up long ago, hence once.

clue.text: Tease a Liberal Democrat with coarse humour

parts.note: to rib someone is to tease them
LD is the abbreviation for a Liberal Democrat, a British political party

explanation.surface: Someone teases a Lib Dem politician with crude jokes.
explanation.definitionFit: Ribald describes humour that is vulgar, bawdy and irreverent.

clue.text: One harshly rules what one can't do to a leopard?

definitions.meaning: a tyrant, an autocrat who governs cruelly

definitions.text: what one can't do to a leopard?
definitions.meaning: a leopard can't change its spots, so one can't remove them

explanation.surface: A tyrant is compared to a leopard that cannot change its spots.
explanation.definitionFit: A tyrant ruling with absolute and often cruel power; the second sense plays on a coined verb.

clue.text: Group of experts criticise the Spanish

parts.note: to pan a play or film is to criticise it harshly
el is Spanish for the

explanation.surface: A committee of experts criticise the Spaniards.
explanation.definitionFit: A small body of specialists gathered to judge or discuss, as on a quiz or inquiry.

clue.text: Distinction of modern artist from 'ere

parts.note: Tracey Emin, the British contemporary artist
from here is hence; dropping the H, as the apostrophe in 'ere does, leaves 'ence

explanation.surface: A modern artist from round these parts gains renown.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Ere is Cockney-style speech with the H dropped; 'from here' is hence, and dropping its H the same way gives ENCE.
explanation.definitionFit: Eminence means fame or high standing, the same as distinction.

clue.text: Station in India left from historic building

indicators.note: left from means the letter for left is taken out of the building

parts.note: a castle is a historic fortified building

explanation.surface: A railway station in India has been abandoned by an old building.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Station' suggests trains, but here it means rank in society.
explanation.definitionFit: A station is one's social rank; in India the hereditary class system divides society into such ranks.

clue.text: Blue feathers

definitions.meaning: the soft fine plumage of birds, used in pillows

explanation.surface: Blue-coloured plumage.
explanation.definitionFit: One sense is miserable, the other is fluffy plumage, as in a duvet filling.

clue.text: The last thing in the Bible that could make cosy appeal

definitions.text: The last thing in the Bible

indicators.note: the letters could make something else, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: A cosy appeal is drawn from the final book of scripture.
explanation.definitionFit: The Apocalypse is another name for the Book of Revelation, the final book of the Bible.

clue.text: Box — one acceptable for horse

parts.note: a stall is a box or compartment for an animal in a stable
I is the Roman numeral for one
on, as in 'that's not on', means acceptable

explanation.surface: A stable box with room for one suitable horse.
explanation.definitionFit: An uncastrated male horse, especially one kept for breeding.

clue.text: Engine stops going by elevated railway

parts.note: an engine dies when it stops running
the El is the American name for an elevated railway, as in Chicago

explanation.surface: A train's engine cuts out as it passes an overhead railway.
explanation.definitionFit: A diesel is a type of compression-ignition engine, or a locomotive using one.
